title: Open restriction and normalized exceptional chart transport with etale witnesses
statement:
Fix the finite purity coefficients [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. For each finite-type $k$-scheme $Z$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], write $C_Z=\nu_Z^*$ for the comparison pullback for $\nu_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] and $\mathcal C(Z)=\mathcal D^+_{\mathrm{et}}(Z,A)$ [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Its objects are triples $(K,K_e,\alpha)$ with $K\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $K_e\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and $\alpha:C_ZK_e\cong K$; its morphisms are all underlying pro-etale morphisms. For a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $v:S\to R$, and a chosen compactification $c$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], let $F_v^c=Rv_{!,e}^c$ be ordinary etale compact support [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $H_v^c$ its ordinary etale right adjoint, and $G_v^c=C_SH_v^cR\nu_{R,*}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; write $Rv_!^c$ for pro-etale compact support [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed].

For every open immersion $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], $Lj^*=j^*$ is exact on both constant-$A$ sites, preserves a cohomological lower bound, and lifts to $\mathcal C(Z)\to\mathcal C(W)$ with witness $j_e^*K_e$ for an input $(K,K_e,\alpha)$. The witness isomorphism is the canonical comparison $C_Wj_e^*K_e\cong j^*C_ZK_e$ followed by $j^*\alpha$. It is natural for all underlying arrows and compatible with identities and successive open restrictions.

Let $V$ be affine of finite type over $k$, let $X$ be any finite-type $k$-scheme, let $f:X\to V$ be a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, and let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an affine open immersion. Choose $d\geq0$, a closed immersion $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^d_V$ and the projection $\pi:T\to V$ [def-sbc-affine-space] with $fj=\pi i$. All these schemes are Noetherian; all displayed maps and composites are separated of finite type and compactifiable. Choose compactifications for the maps defining $F_f,H_f,F_i,H_i,F_\pi,H_\pi$ above, and suppress their superscripts. For every $N_e\in D^+(V_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the objects
$$Q=j_e^*H_fN_e,\qquad B=H_iH_\pi N_e$$
belong to $D^+(U_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. There is a natural isomorphism $a:Q\xrightarrow{\sim}B$ in that derived category, uniquely normalized by the natural Hom chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(H,Q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_{e!}H,H_fN_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_fj_{e!}H,N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_\pi i_{e*}H,N_e)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)$$
for every bounded-below $H$ on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$: the map on Hom sets is postcomposition with $a$, using the ordinary adjunctions and normalized compact-support compositor. Here Hom sets are taken in the ordinary etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $j_e^*$ is etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], $j_{e!}$ is etale extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] and $i_{e*}$ is etale direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

For every $N=(N,N_e,\beta)\in\mathcal C(V)$, the witness-unit identifications give $G_fN\cong C_XH_fN_e$, $G_\pi N\cong C_TH_\pi N_e$, and $G_iG_\pi N\cong C_UH_iH_\pi N_e$; the last identification uses the comparison unit at the bounded-below object $H_\pi N_e$. Under these identifications and the open pullback comparison, $C_Ua$ gives a natural isomorphism
$$Lj^*G_f\cong G_iG_\pi:\mathcal C(V)\longrightarrow\mathcal C(U).$$
Its source has etale witness $Q$ and its target has etale witness $B$; naturality holds for every underlying pro-etale morphism in $\mathcal C(V)$. No separatedness of $X$ over $k$, or bounded constructibility of $N$ or any exceptional image, is required.

proof.text: First check the geometry. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are zero and the whole ring. Thus $X,V$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [def-sbc-affine-space], $T=\operatorname{Spec}R[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ and $\pi$ is induced by the inclusion of constants. This is a finite-type morphism directly by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]: it is affine with finitely generated coordinate algebra. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to $\pi$ shows $T$ Noetherian. All four schemes are quasi-compact; they are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text: For every affine open $O\subseteq X$, $j^{-1}(O)=U\cap O$ is an open subscheme of the Noetherian scheme $X$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Thus $j$ is quasi-compact and is finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The closed immersion $i$ is proper, in particular separated finite type, by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. The morphisms $j,\pi,i$ and the composite $fj=\pi i$ have affine sources, so are separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]; $f$ is separated by hypothesis. Finite type for the composites, and for $T$ and $U$ over $k$, follows from [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change]. The identity of $V$ has both properties directly. All their targets are qcqs by step 1, so [thm-nagata-compactification] applies to every one of these separated finite-type maps. No separatedness hypothesis on $X$ over $k$ is invoked.

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text: For any open $j:W\hookrightarrow Z$, [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] make the two constant-$A$ inverse images exact. Applied termwise they preserve quasi-isomorphisms, and $\mathcal H^r(j^*K)=j^*\mathcal H^r(K)$ follows by applying exactness to kernels and images. Hence $Lj^*=j^*$ and a lower bound is preserved. Write $\kappa_j:C_Wj_e^*\cong j^*C_Z$ for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. For $(K,K_e,\alpha)$ choose witness $j_e^*K_e$ with isomorphism $j^*\alpha\circ\kappa_{j,K_e}$. On an arrow use $j^*$ of its underlying arrow; [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory] puts no witness condition on arrows, so the identity and composition laws follow from those of $j^*$. For successive opens $h,j$, the coherence of $\kappa$ says, after the canonical pullback associators, $\kappa_{jh}=(h^*\kappa_j)\circ(\kappa_h j_e^*)$. Thus the successive witness isomorphism is $(jh)^*\alpha\circ\kappa_{jh}$; the identity comparison gives the identity restriction. This also proves the requested open-restriction coherence.

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text: For $v=f,i,\pi$, apply [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint] at its chosen compactification, legitimate by steps 1–2. Its evaluation comparison and uniform lower bound imply that the ordinary finite-level adjoint $H_v$ preserves bounded-below objects: for $L\in D^{\geq a}((\operatorname{target}v)_{\mathrm{et}},A_n)$, form the strict system with value $L$ at every $m\geq n$, as an $A_m$-complex through $A_m\to A_n$, identity transition maps there, and value zero at $m<n$. It is in $D^{\geq a}$ since system cohomology is levelwise. The cited bound puts its adjoint image in $D^{\geq a-c_v}$; evaluation at $n$ is $H_vL$. In particular $H_fN_e,H_\pi N_e,H_iH_\pi N_e$ are bounded below, and step 3 puts $Q=j_e^*H_fN_e$ in $D^+$. Thus $B$ and $Q$ can both serve as test objects in the bounded-below Hom chain. The comparison pullbacks of all these objects are bounded below by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact].

source.place: Step 1, bounded-below prerequisites; Zheng, Constructions 5.14–5.15 and Lemma 5.22 via the existing coefficient-system adjoint theorem

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-etale-chart-adjoint-comparison] with its $Y=V$, $s=j$, $v=\mathrm{id}_V$, $P=T$, $p=\pi$ and $K=N_e$. Steps 1–2 verify its Noetherian, separated finite-type and compactification hypotheses, and its factorization equality is exactly $fj=\pi i$. Take the inverse of its stated Hom bijection and remove the identity-open adjunction. This gives $\Theta_H:\operatorname{Hom}(H,Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(H,B)$, natural in $H,N_e$, by the exact chain in the item: open extension/restriction adjunction, $F_f\dashv H_f$, the specified normalized compact-support compositor, then the closed and projection adjunctions. Thus the normalization comes from this cited chain, including its $i_{e*}$, rather than from an arbitrary isomorphism between the representing objects.

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text: Set $a=\Theta_Q(1_Q):Q\to B$ and $b=\Theta_B^{-1}(1_B):B\to Q$. These evaluations are allowed by step 4. Naturality in the test object gives $\Theta_H(t)=a\circ t$ and $\Theta_H^{-1}(z)=b\circ z$. The inverse identities for $\Theta$ therefore give $a\circ b=1_B$ and $b\circ a=1_Q$. Any morphism inducing this Hom chain equals $\Theta_Q(1_Q)$, proving uniqueness with the required normalization. For $\phi:N_e\to N'_e$, naturality of step 5 evaluated at $1_Q$ gives $H_iH_\pi(\phi)\circ a_{N_e}=a_{N'_e}\circ j_e^*H_f(\phi)$. Hence $a$ is a natural derived isomorphism.

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text:
Put $R_Z=R\nu_{Z,*}$ and let $\eta_Z:1\to R_ZC_Z$ be the natural invertible unit of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. For a witnessed input $(N,N_e,\beta)$, the map $u_N=R_V(\beta)\circ\eta_{V,N_e}:N_e\xrightarrow{\sim}R_VN$ is invertible. For $v=f,\pi$ set $s_{v,N}=C_{\operatorname{source}v}H_v(u_N)$, an isomorphism $C_{\operatorname{source}v}H_vN_e\to G_vN$ by the finite formula of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Define
$$q_N=j^*s_{f,N}\circ\kappa_{j,H_fN_e}:C_UQ\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*G_fN,$$
$$t_N=C_UH_i\bigl(R_T(s_{\pi,N})\circ\eta_{T,H_\pi N_e}\bigr):C_UB\xrightarrow{\sim}G_iG_\pi N.$$
The second unit is invertible because $H_\pi N_e\in D^+$ by step 4. All their comparison pullbacks lie in $D^+$ by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact], and the pullback comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Thus the asserted underlying chart map is precisely $t_N\circ C_U(a_{N_e})\circ q_N^{-1}$. Its source witness is $(Q,q_N)$ and its target witness is $(B,t_N)$, so it and its inverse are arrows of the induced category [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory].

source.place: Step 1, chart adjoints; expanded normalized witnessed argument in Q24 report, returned Steps 6–9

proof.text:
Let $h:(N,N_e,\beta)\to(N',N'_e,\beta')$ be any underlying pro-etale arrow. By full faithfulness of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] there is a unique $\phi:N_e\to N'_e$ with $C_V\phi=(\beta')^{-1}h\beta$. Naturality of the unit gives the explicit equation
$$R_V(h)R_V(\beta)\eta_{N_e}=R_V(\beta')R_V(C_V\phi)\eta_{N_e}=R_V(\beta')\eta_{N'_e}\phi.$$
Applying $C H_v$ yields $G_v(h)s_{v,N}=s_{v,N'}C H_v(\phi)$. Combining this equation for $v=f$ with the naturality of $\kappa_j$ from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] proves $j^*G_f(h)q_N=q_{N'}C_U(j_e^*H_f\phi)$. The same equation for $v=\pi$, followed by unit naturality on $T$ at $H_\pi\phi$, proves $G_iG_\pi(h)t_N=t_{N'}C_U(H_iH_\pi\phi)$. Substituting the naturality equation for $a$ from step 6 proves naturality of $t_N C_U(a)q_N^{-1}$ for this arbitrary $h$. Together with step 3 this proves every asserted lift and coherence. The argument uses arbitrary $D^+$ witnesses throughout, without a constructibility or finite-Tor hypothesis.
